E1: (1) A ProximityPrompt only works when parented to a BasePart, an Attachment, or a Model (a Model uses its PrimaryPart/pivot for position). Under a Folder it has no world position, so it never shows. Fix: move it into a part of the machine (or an Attachment on the button part), or parent it to the Model and set VendingMachine.PrimaryPart. (2) RequiresLineOfSight defaults to true: the engine raycasts from the camera to the prompt, and the glass case blocks that ray, so the prompt is suppressed. Fix: set RequiresLineOfSight = false on the lever prompt, or move the prompt to a part/attachment outside the glass (or make the glass non-queryable if nothing else needs to hit it).
E2: AlwaysOnTop = false: the gui is then depth-tested, so walls occlude it (true draws over all 3D). MaxDistance = 100: the billboard stops rendering beyond 100 studs from the camera (default 0 = infinite). Size: use scale instead of offset, e.g. UDim2.fromScale(4, 1). On a BillboardGui, scale components are measured in studs, so the tag is a fixed world size and shrinks with distance; offset is fixed screen pixels, which is why it never shrinks. Optionally keep a small offset part or use SizeOffset/StudsOffset for placement, and LightInfluence = 0 so it stays readable. Use TextScaled on the label so text fits the scaled frame.
E3:
CharacterAutoLoads = false turns off all automatic spawning: no character on join and no respawn after death. RespawnTime only applies to the automatic respawn, so it does nothing now. You must spawn manually with Player:LoadCharacter() (or LoadCharacterAsync where available) on the server:
```lua
local Players = game:GetService('Players')
Players.CharacterAutoLoads = false
local function onPlayer(p)
  p.CharacterAdded:Connect(function(char)
    char:WaitForChild('Humanoid').Died:Connect(function()
      task.delay(3, function()
        if p.Parent then p:LoadCharacter() end
      end)
    end)
  end)
  p:LoadCharacter()
end
Players.PlayerAdded:Connect(onPlayer)
for _, p in Players:GetPlayers() do task.spawn(onPlayer, p) end
```
For rounds, call LoadCharacter when the round logic wants the player in instead of on death.
E4: CanQuery = false removes a part from ALL spatial queries (raycasts, GetPartsInPart, etc.), regardless of RaycastParams filters, so the ray can never hit it. CanCollide = false alone is enough to let players walk through, and raycasts hit non-collidable parts by default (RespectCanCollide is false). Fix: set CanQuery = true on the glass (keep CanCollide = false). If you need finer control, use collision groups for walk-through and a RaycastParams filter / CollisionGroup on the ray, e.g. exclude player characters.
E5: Clone() returns nil when the instance's Archivable is false, so g is nil and g:PivotTo errors. Destroy() sets Parent to nil and locks it permanently (also disconnects connections and marks it for cleanup), so the destroyed template can never be reparented: 'Parent property is locked'. Correct pattern: keep the template in ServerStorage (or ReplicatedStorage) with Archivable = true (set it back, or set template.Archivable = true in code before cloning), never parent or destroy the template, clone a fresh copy for each spawn, and Destroy() the clone when that goblin dies (or use a pool of clones that you reparent to nil/storage instead of destroying, if you want reuse).

```lua
local function swing(attacker)
  local char = attacker.Character
  local hrp = char and char:FindFirstChild('HumanoidRootPart')
  if not hrp then return end
  local cf = hrp.CFrame * CFrame.new(0, 0, -3)
  local params = OverlapParams.new()
  params.FilterType = Enum.RaycastFilterType.Exclude
  params.FilterDescendantsInstances = { char }
  local hit = {}
  for _, part in workspace:GetPartBoundsInBox(cf, Vector3.new(6, 5, 6), params) do
    local model = part:FindFirstAncestorOfClass('Model')
    local hum = model and model:FindFirstChildOfClass('Humanoid')
    if hum and not hit[hum] and hum.Health > 0 then
      hit[hum] = true
      hum:TakeDamage(20)
    end
  end
end
```
The hit set guarantees one hit per humanoid per swing. Caveat: GetPartBoundsInBox tests the parts' axis-aligned bounding boxes, not true geometry, so it can over-report (rotated/odd-shaped parts). Use GetPartsInPart with a box hitbox part for exact geometry at higher cost. Also the server sees positions with latency, so validate swing cooldown/range server-side.

E12: Per-server budgets (per minute): GetAsync 60 + 10 x players; Set/Update/Increment/Remove (write) 60 + 10 x players; with 40 players that is 460/min each. UpdateAsync consumes both a read and a write budget. GetSorted/ordered and ListKeys have their own budgets. Check DataStoreService:GetRequestBudgetForRequestType before bursts. Your load: 40 autosaves/min + leaves is far under budget. Per-key limits: at most one write to the same key every 6 seconds (more queue/throttle); value max 4 MB (per key, serialized JSON); key name max 50 chars; datastore name max 50 chars. Also: requests over budget go into a throttle queue that can fill and error, so stagger autosaves (don't save all 40 in the same tick), skip saving unchanged data, pcall + retry with backoff, use session locking for cross-server safety, and use BindToClose to save on shutdown (about 30 s window). Keep experience-wide storage and throughput limits in mind (newer per-experience limits apply).

E15: Missing parts: with streaming, parts of a normal model stream in independently, so a LocalScript can see a partial model. Set the building Model.ModelStreamingMode = Atomic: the model and all its descendants stream in together, so once the model exists (WaitForChild on the model) every part is there. Trade-off: the whole model streams as a unit (more data at once, streams out as a unit). Scoreboard: ModelStreamingMode = Persistent: it is sent at join and never streamed out on any client. Trade-off: costs memory and join bandwidth on every client, so use sparingly; PersistentPerPlayer + Model:AddPersistentPlayer(player) limits it to specific players. Other tools: Player:RequestStreamAroundAsync(position) on the server to preload an area before teleporting/showing something; StreamingMinRadius/StreamingTargetRadius control how much is kept (bigger = more memory); StreamOutBehavior (Opportunistic vs LowMemory); StreamingIntegrityMode to pause when the player's area isn't loaded. Client code should always handle instances appearing/disappearing (ChildAdded, CollectionService tag signals) rather than assuming they exist.
E16: Aim direction: yes, switch to UnreliableRemoteEvent. It is sent often, only the latest value matters, and dropped/out-of-order packets are harmless (the next update replaces it); it also avoids reliable-queue head-of-line delays. Hits: no, keep a reliable RemoteEvent; a lost hit report means lost damage, and the server must still validate it (rate, distance, line of sight). E17:
```lua
-- layout: u16 id (2) + 3 x f32 (12) = 14 bytes
local function pack(id: number, pos: Vector3): buffer
  local b = buffer.create(14)
  buffer.writeu16(b, 0, id)
  buffer.writef32(b, 2, pos.X)
  buffer.writef32(b, 6, pos.Y)
  buffer.writef32(b, 10, pos.Z)
  return b
end
local function unpack(b: buffer): (number, Vector3)
  if buffer.len(b) ~= 14 then error('bad packet') end
  local id = buffer.readu16(b, 0)
  return id, Vector3.new(buffer.readf32(b, 2), buffer.readf32(b, 6), buffer.readf32(b, 10))
end
-- sender: remote:FireAllClients(pack(id, pos))
-- receiver: remote.OnClientEvent:Connect(function(b) local id, pos = unpack(b) end)
```
Rules: buffers are fixed-size (buffer.create(n), zero-filled, cannot grow); offsets are 0-based byte offsets; reads/writes out of bounds throw; multi-byte values are little-endian; integer writes wrap/truncate to the width (u16 = 0..65535); f32 loses precision vs Luau's f64 numbers; buffers are copied when sent through remotes. Validate length on the receiver (an exploiter can send any buffer).
E18: Every unanchored assembly has a network owner that simulates its physics: the server or one client. By default the engine assigns ownership automatically (usually to the nearest player), and a seated driver normally gets ownership of the vehicle assembly. Stutter happens when ownership flips between server and clients (e.g. other players nearby, or the server owning it), so the driver's input has a round-trip delay. Fix on the server: when VehicleSeat.Occupant changes, call seat:SetNetworkOwner(player) (on any part of the welded assembly; it applies to the whole assembly; must not be anchored) and SetNetworkOwner(nil) or SetNetworkOwnershipAuto() when they leave. Kill brick: when a client owns the cart, the cart's physics/touches are computed on that client and replicated; the server sees interpolated, delayed positions, so server Touched can fire late, at odd positions, or be spoofed by exploiters. Server-side kill logic should check the touching part belongs to a character (GetPlayerFromCharacter / Humanoid) and ignore cart parts, or use server spatial queries and sanity checks rather than trusting client-simulated contacts.

Storage: a per-experience storage quota (about 100 MB + 1 MB per lifetime user) is enforced, with usage visible in the Creator Dashboard; exceeding it blocks writes. Access: besides per-server budgets (60 + 10 x players/min), there are experience-wide throughput limits per data store/key and per-request-type, scaled by concurrent users, with errors when exceeded. What to do: keep save data compact (no redundant fields, shorter keys, serialize efficiently), delete stale data (RemoveAsync for removed features, GDPR requests, old versions/backups you no longer need, avoid unnecessary per-save copies), avoid per-event writes (cache in memory, autosave on an interval, save on leave/BindToClose), use UpdateAsync with retries and exponential backoff on throttling errors, check GetRequestBudgetForRequestType, and monitor the Data Stores observability dashboard.
E20:
I am not confident of the exact 2026 property names. The classic model: FilterDescendantsInstances + FilterType (Include or Exclude) is one list with one mode, so you cannot express 'include Map but exclude Map.Glass' in a single list. The newer additions let you combine inclusion and exclusion (separate include/exclude lists, or filtering by collision group/tags), where exclusion takes precedence over inclusion. Setup with the classic API that works regardless:
```lua
local params = RaycastParams.new()
params.FilterType = Enum.RaycastFilterType.Include
params.FilterDescendantsInstances = { workspace.Map }
local function cast(origin, dir)
  local r = workspace:Raycast(origin, dir, params)
  while r and r.Instance:IsDescendantOf(workspace.Map.Glass) do
    origin = r.Position + dir.Unit * 0.01
    dir = dir - (r.Position - origin)
    r = workspace:Raycast(origin, dir, params)
  end
  return r
end
```
Or put the glass in a collision group the ray's params.CollisionGroup doesn't collide with. With the new dual filter you would just include workspace.Map and exclude workspace.Map.Glass in one params object.

Not fully certain of the exact signature; as I understand it: BindReceiptHandler lets you register a handler for specific developer product(s) instead of one global ProcessReceipt callback. Shape: MarketplaceService:BindReceiptHandler(productId, function(receiptInfo) ... return Enum.ProductPurchaseDecision.PurchaseGranted end). The handler gets the same receiptInfo (PlayerId, ProductId, PurchaseId, CurrencySpent...) and returns PurchaseGranted only after the grant is durably saved, else NotProcessedYet so Roblox retries. Each script binds only its own product IDs, so several systems can coexist (no single giant ProcessReceipt dispatcher). Receipts for products with a bound handler go to that handler; unbound products fall back to ProcessReceipt; don't handle the same product in both. Still be idempotent (record PurchaseId).

  local plr = game.Players:GetPlayerByUserId(r.PlayerId)
  if not plr then return Enum.ProductPurchaseDecision.NotProcessedYet end
  local ok = grantCoins(plr, 100, r.PurchaseId)
  return ok and Enum.ProductPurchaseDecision.PurchaseGranted or Enum.ProductPurchaseDecision.NotProcessedYet

E24: Luau added math.lerp, plus math.isnan, math.isinf and math.isfinite (math.map was added a bit earlier, alongside math.clamp/sign/round/noise). Signatures: math.lerp(a: number, b: number, t: number): number -- returns a + (b - a) * t, exact at t = 1 (returns b) and monotonic; math.map(x: number, inMin: number, inMax: number, outMin: number, outMax: number): number -- remaps x from [inMin, inMax] to [outMin, outMax] (not clamped). Example: math.map(50, 0, 100, 0, 1) == 0.5; math.lerp(10, 20, 0.25) == 12.5. Use these instead of hand-written helpers; they are native and faster. Note Vector3/CFrame/Color3 still use their own :Lerp methods.
